description: Test results pasted as console text instead of XML: Maven Surefire console output for StockLevelServiceTest ("Tests run: 12, Failures: 1, Errors: 0, Skipped: 1 ... <<< FAILURE! - in ..." plus an "[ERROR] method(class)  Time elapsed ... <<< FAILURE!" line) and Gradle test logging for ReorderPolicyTest ("ReorderPolicyTest > method() PASSED / FAILED / SKIPPED", including parameterized and @Nested display names). The matching JUnit 5 test code for both classes is pasted; failure line numbers in the logs point at the real assertion lines. No production code, JaCoCo or scope.

quality.note: @Disabled("waiting for the warehouse API sandbox; see INV-102").

notes: Top-level results aggregate both result pastes (12 + 7 executions); per-paste numbers are in the paste-level "results" extension key. results.failed uses "<fully-qualified class>.<method name>" without parameters or parentheses.

Maven paste: "Tests run: 12" appears twice (per-class line and the final summary) and must not be double-counted. 12 = 9 plain test methods + 3 rejectsMalformedSku invocations; the skipped one is the @Disabled syncsWithWarehouse. The failing method is given as "shouldFlagLowStockAtThreshold(com.acme.inventory.StockLevelServiceTest)" and again as "StockLevelServiceTest.shouldFlagLowStockAtThreshold:63"; line 63 of 01-test-StockLevelServiceTest.txt is its assertTrue.

Gradle paste: the class is shown by simple name only ("ReorderPolicyTest > ..."); the FQCN com.acme.inventory.ReorderPolicyTest comes from the pasted test code. Method names carry "()" or a parameter-type list "(int, int)"; parameterized invocations add "> [n] args"; the @Nested class appears by its @DisplayName ("Seasonal items"), not by its class name Seasonal. "7 tests completed, 1 failed, 1 skipped" is the authoritative total. The failure location ReorderPolicyTest.java:24 is the real assertion line.
The Gradle output has no PASSED/FAILED line for the nested class itself and no per-test timing; the Maven output only lists failures individually (passing tests are not named).
Neither console format reports errors separately for these runs: errors = 0 in both.
coverageStatus is an extension key: no JaCoCo was pasted, so coverage is NOT VERIFIED; passing tests are not evidence of coverage.
ReorderPolicyTest.legacyMinimumTable contains a // comment with braces and the text "@Test" (line 46) that must not be counted as an annotation.

shouldFlagLowStockAtThreshold is a genuine boundary test (on-hand == threshold) and it is the one that fails; the test is not defective, it exposes a likely "<" vs "<=" bug in production code that is not pasted.
